description: Six-channel gate and CV sequencer of 128 steps played in from one big button; it runs whenever its clock runs and has no run control of its own

params.text: Chooses which of the six channels every button acts on; it can be turned while the sequencer runs and takes effect at once
Sets how many steps the current channel plays before it loops round, 1 to 128
Sets the chance that the gate of the step about to be reached is flipped in the current channel: at the left end nothing changes, at the right end every step is flipped
Returns every channel to its first step
Turns off every gate of the current channel and returns all of its stored voltages to C4
Switches the current channel between its two stored sequences
Clears the gate at the current step while it is held down, so holding it through several steps clears them all
Plays a gate on every clock pulse of the current channel while it is held down, starting on the next pulse
Turns on the gate of the current step in the current channel and stores the voltage at CV IN as that step's CV
With this off, the gates played by FILL sound but are not written into the sequence
Quantizes the big button and DEL to the nearest beat rather than the beat last reached; it needs a steady clock of at least 30 BPM, and switches itself off internally below that
Samples each channel's CV output on that channel's own gate, so the voltage changes only as a gate fires
Advances the sequencer one step for each press, for programming a sequence without a running clock
Switches the display between the length of the current channel and the step it has reached

inputs.text: Advances the sequencer one step per pulse; stopping this clock is the only way to stop the sequencer
Chooses the channel from a voltage, 0-10V spread over the six channels
A trigger here turns on the gate of the current step and stores the voltage at CV IN as that step's CV
Added to the LEN knob, 10V covering the whole 128 steps
Added to the RND knob after being divided by ten, so 10V reaches full probability with the knob at its left end
A trigger here returns every channel to its first step
A trigger here turns off every gate of the current channel and returns all of its stored voltages to C4
A trigger here switches the current channel between its two stored sequences
Above 0.5V here clears the gate at the current step, and goes on clearing each step while it stays high
Above 0.5V here plays a gate on every clock pulse of the current channel while it stays high
The voltage taken into a step when the big button is pressed, and taken on every clock pulse while FILL runs with MEM on, which is how the module is used as a CV recorder

outputs.text: The clock pulse itself on each step of that channel that holds a gate
The stored voltage of the step that channel has reached

menu: Retrigger gates on reset — holds the gate outputs low for 1ms after a reset so a trigger-sensitive target fires again; the choices are No and Yes
Big and Del on next step — registers every big button and DEL press on the step after the current one, and SNAP then has no effect
Metronome light — sets how often the big button's light blinks as a metronome: Every clock, /2, /4, /8, or Full length
Portable sequence — holds Copy sequence and Paste sequence, which move the current channel's sequence between this module and other sequencers that support the format

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

inputs.6: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.7: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.8: high above 0.5V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.9: high above 0.5V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.10: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
